findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as object keys, evaluating to `"[object Object]"`
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed property names `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate at runtime to the literal string key `"[object Object]"`. Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, parsing any token response with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips the actual expiry field (e.g. `expires_in` or `expiry_date`) and every other field except `access_token`. To allow arbitrary additional fields or numeric expiry fields, use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(...)` instead of computed keys on `z.string()`.

findings.title: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` return wrapper is saved directly as the credential `key` in the database
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed data itself. In `GoogleCalendarService`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. This overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, which corrupts the stored credential and causes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw a validation error on every subsequent request.

findings.title: `prisma` is used without being imported and refreshed `access_token` is never passed to `jsforce.Connection`
findings.body: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in this file, causing a `ReferenceError` at runtime and breaking type-checking; (2) the token refresh `fetch` on line 75 does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential syncing is bypassed; and (3) after refreshing the token, `new jsforce.Connection` on line 106 still passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, and `fetch` response is incompatible with `axios` response
findings.body: In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `credentialId` (`credential.id`) is passed as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`, sending the credential ID instead of the user ID as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. Additionally, when credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` object, whereas the callback uses `axios.post` which returns `{ data: ... }`. Accessing `tokenInfo.data.error` on line 96 will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')` whenever syncing is enabled. The same `axios` vs `fetch` response mismatch also affects `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94), `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217), and `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192, where the SDK returns the token object directly rather than a `Response`).
